risk_if_not_implemented: Without Automated Software & Firmware Updates, embedded and IoT technologies may operate with unknown, insecure or unmonitored configurations, creating exploitable footholds. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector) (R-BC-4), Exposure from Unaddressed Vulnerabilities (R-EX-6), System / Service Compromise (R-EX-7), Incident Persistence / Recurrence (R-IR-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Geopolitical Conflict / Government Intervention (MT-18).

compensating_control_1.name: Vulnerability Scanning
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to detect vulnerabilities and configuration errors by routine vulnerability scanning of systems and applications.
compensating_control_1.justification: Vulnerability Scanning (VPM-12) provides vulnerability management that compensates for the absence of Automated Software & Firmware Updates (VPM-08.1) by reducing the exploitable attack surface by addressing known weaknesses before they are leveraged. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Software & Firmware Patching
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to conduct software patching for all deployed Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including firmware.
compensating_control_2.justification: Software & Firmware Patching (VPM-08) provides vulnerability management that compensates for the absence of Automated Software & Firmware Updates (VPM-08.1) by reducing the exploitable attack surface by addressing known weaknesses before they are leveraged. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
